A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from Hybrid Preference Optimization (HPO) to Unified Preference Optimization (UPO). Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HPO experiments measuring preference alignment, safety and readability across five language models, plus ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original alignment experiments and reports additional comparisons, Pareto tradeoffs, robustness tests and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The preference objective, advantage-weighted likelihood update and expectile value head are retained. However, the specified safety reward changes from max_i(1-r_i) in v1 Equation 14 to 1-max_i(r_i) in v3 Equation 12, changing the auxiliary training target as written. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a formula correction.

E1.justification: The Anthropic HH, OpenAssistant and SHP dialogue coverage is retained. v3 Appendix A.4.6 adds explicit verbosity control alongside readability and safety. Although Appendix A.4.7 invokes AlpacaEval, its results passage explicitly describes evaluation on the retained OASST/SHP/HH data, rather than establishing a separate new corpus.

E2.justification: v3 adds DRO-V and auxiliary-objective PPO (aoPPO), and extends MODPO and A-LOL from v1's LLAMA-13B ablation comparison into the main five-model comparisons. Appendix A.4.10 adds ConDPO. The earlier weighted-KTO and standalone L_pi comparisons disappear; the original preference-only baselines remain.

E3.justification: Safety evaluation changes from the top 5% unsafe prompts to top 10%, top 20% and full-set evaluations, with explicit tolerance thresholds. Readability reporting shifts from ninth-grade violations to reward and mean grade level. The stated default weights reverse from 0.95 readability/0.05 safety to 0.05/0.95. New experiments introduce weight grids, random-reward controls and AlpacaEval judging; the original model suite and 512-prompt setting remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained readability, response-length and hyperparameter analyses, v3 adds Pareto tradeoffs, an additional verbosity objective, a DPO-based UPO test, DRO-V gradient/regularization analysis, uniformly random auxiliary rewards, evaluator length-bias analysis and computational profiling. It also expands qualitative cases while removing v1's standalone RL-only and weighted-KTO ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions already report values with plus/minus uncertainty. v3 additionally reports significance thresholds for performance comparisons and p-values for length correlations. Neither version clearly specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or the statistical tests used; changed error-bar values alone do not establish a new estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Reported HPO/UPO LLAMA-7B GPT-4 scores change from 41.5 to 44.8, while most original comparator scores remain unchanged. MODPO's LLAMA-13B score changes from 0.0 in v1 Table 3 to 38.8 in v3 Table 2 under the revised experimental description. Extensive new baseline, Pareto, robustness and efficiency results appear. Revised reward settings and evaluation definitions prevent treating all numerical changes as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the formal OPT framework and Theorem A.2 claiming KTO optimality under balanced-label assumptions. It generalizes v1's Bradley-Terry optimum theorem to OPT objectives and adds gradient arguments for MODPO, UPO and competing RL methods, plus random-reward derivations. These substantially extend the retained ranking bound and KL derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains combining preference optimization with efficient, stable auxiliary-reward optimization while preserving alignment quality. v3 adds explicit claims about avoiding specialized data and reference-model or paired-data requirements, conditional on the chosen base technique, and foregrounds practical computational scalability. The HPO-to-UPO renaming itself does not change the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving conflicting preference/auxiliary rankings, sparse rewards, importance weights and DRO-V regularization. It discusses evaluator length bias, classifier-based safety evaluation, model-selection boundaries, imperfect weight-to-outcome control and harmful repurposing. These substantially expand v1's discussion of rambling and difficulty choosing objective weights.

D1.justification: The existing code sketch, model families, optimizer, learning rate and hardware disclosures are retained. v3 newly identifies textstat.text_standard, gradient clipping at 10, comparator tuning, ConDPO conditioning details and timing/memory measurement procedures. Runtime estimates are revised, including GPT-4 evaluation from roughly 30 to 60 minutes. Newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to previously run experiments.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against contemporary offline RL, on-policy RL and conditional or multi-objective preference methods, including DRO-V, REBEL, RLOO, ULMA and controllable preference optimization. New comparative properties and arguments emphasize limitations of binary objectives and computational costs. These are substantive additions beyond publication-year and citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively revised. The method gains separate derivation and advantages subsections, experiments are reorganized around methodology, tradeoffs and efficiency, and the original appendices A-D become a substantially expanded, nested Appendix A.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the method diagram, expands the main comparison table and replaces the two-part auxiliary table with four panels. It adds method-property, Pareto, qualitative-example and efficiency displays, and revises the safety plots. The readability histogram and response-length analysis move to the appendix, with the latter gaining A-LOL. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v1's multi-objective superiority rested largely on preference-only baselines and a MODPO run that collapsed. v3 supplies tuned multi-objective comparisons across five models, Pareto tradeoffs, cost measurements and targeted robustness analyses, substantially strengthening the central empirical case. Important limits remain: significance-test procedures are unspecified, and the new KTO proof replaces optimization of E[v] with E[Psi(v)] without establishing equivalence. Revised rewards and metrics also preclude interpreting every numerical change as a performance improvement.
